summary: Headquarters lookout of the J. Clark Salyer NWR, a 110-ft steel tower moved to Rugby's Prairie Village Museum in 1992; build year not found.

events.note: Moved from the refuge headquarters to the Prairie Village Museum in Rugby; the register gives a cost of $12,000 after a local fundraising campaign
Registered March 25, 2020 as US 1414, ND 2; nominated by Lawrence Kuracina

corrections.current: None relocated (Moved from Salyer NWR – HQ to Rugby.)
corrections.proposed: 1992 relocated: moved from the Salyer NWR headquarters to the Prairie Village Museum, Rugby
corrections.why: The relocation entry gives no year and reads 'None'; the register and West Lookouts both date the move to 1992.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: West Lookouts writes the refuge as 'Sayler'; the register and the Fish and Wildlife Service use 'Salyer'. This history uses Salyer.

The register says the tower was one of four at the refuge without naming the unit; West Lookouts and the Forest Fire Lookout Association tie it to the headquarters site, so it is treated as the headquarters tower.

notes_for_editor: Build year and builder not found in any source reached (WebSearch and the Wikipedia refuge page had no tower entry). Relocation (1992), cost and registration are well sourced. Access is unconfirmed: the museum's visitor page does not mention the tower, so no access key was set. Height 33.5 m is our conversion of the register's 110 ft. Do not confuse with the separate Northern Lights Tower, an 88.5-ft steel sculpture in Rugby that the museum page also describes. LOC HAER photos returned 403, so no new photo was recorded.
